Dealer Selling 2020 Ford GT With 3,000 Miles and You're Very Lucky if You Can Afford It
13 photos
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago
It’s been four years since the Ford GT story ended, and so far, the Blue Oval hasn’t announced anything about a possible successor to its iconic supercar.
The last example of the second generation rolled off the line north of the US border, at Markham, Ontario, Canada, in late 2022, thus marking the end of an era. And while there is no successor anywhere in sight, those who want a blue-blooded GT from the Dearborn-based automaker in their garage have nothing else to do than search the used car market for that example that looks perfect to them.
Does the one pictured in the gallery tick this box? Well, in that case, you are in luck, because it is indeed searching for a new home on the used car market in the States. This Ford GT features a yellow paint finish on the outside, has racing strips in black with a gray center stretching across its length, from the front bumper to the rear hood and wing, and benefits from other black details on the lower parts of the body and not only.
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago The wheels may appear black too, but upon closer inspection, you will see that they have been made of carbon fiber, and actually feature a dry look. The EcoBoost engine is visible at the rear even without popping the hood open, courtesy of the transparent cover. And it is a twin-turbocharged 3.5-liter V6, in case you forgot, it initially pumped out 647 horsepower (483 kW/656 ps).
From the 2020 model year onward , the engine was tuned to produce 660 horsepower (492 kW669 ps). With no modifications whatsoever, the second-generation Ford GT brags about running the standing quarter mile in 10.6 seconds. The 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) sprint is a 2.9-second affair, and the top speed stands at 216 mph (348 kph). Not too shabby.
A look inside the pictured Ford GT reveals that the cockpit has been dressed in black Alcantara. You can see the upholstery on the seats, steering wheel, lower and upper parts of the dashboard panel, and other components. Carbon fiber trim is also on deck, and so is white stitching for some contrast.
As mentioned in the title, this American supercar is a 2020 model year, and at the time of cataloging, it had around 3,000 miles (~4,800 km) or so on the odometer. That’s what the vendor, @motorcarsofchicago on Instagram, claims. The dealer accepts trades, offers financing, and asks for $1,099,995 for the Ford GT in question, and that’s why we said that you are very lucky if you can afford this thing.
But if you had all the money in the world, would you pay $1.1 million for this low-mileage example? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Motor Cars of Chicago (@motorcarsofchicago)
